_rule: Declared exceptions to exact reproduction. Each entry names a block, a substring of the reference line, the positions of the tolerated numbers on that line (0-based, negative counts from the end), and either 'upper' (the number must stay below the bound the check actually claims, in this run and in the reference) or 'rel' (relative closeness), with the reason. Only lines that measure numerical noise qualify, and only after a run on another machine has shown the noise. Keep this list short: a result that moves across machines is a finding, not a tolerance.

V25.why: Forward differences with h = 1e-7 are dominated by round-off. On a GitHub runner (first CI runs, 2026-09-26) the VPG relative error read 7.2e-05 against the reference 4.0e-05, and the Gibbs error 8.6e-07 against 8.7e-07. The check claims agreement with the covariance formulas to finite-difference accuracy. The bounds sit well above the noise and three orders of magnitude or more below the O(0.1-1) quantities being compared.

V33.why: Central differences with h = 1e-6 are dominated by round-off, and their digits depend on the CPU's SIMD path. Disabling AVX-512 locally moves the relative error from 5.5e-05 to 5.8e-05 and leaves every other V33 line unchanged. The first CI run on a GitHub runner also failed V33. The check claims that d/dt E G equals Var G to finite-difference accuracy. The bounds sit far above the noise and far below Var.
